title: Gas Detector
subtitle: MQ-135 Gas and Air Quality Leakage Detection System with LCD & Buzzer Alarm
author: Tinkering Lab
desc: Detect hazardous gas leaks and harmful air pollutants in real-time using an MQ-135 sensor, I2C LCD display, LED, and buzzer alert system.
fullDesc: The Gas Detector project uses an MQ-135 gas sensor interfaced with an Arduino Uno to continuously monitor ambient air for hazardous gases such as ammonia, benzene, alcohol, smoke, and CO2. When gas concentrations exceed a safe threshold, the system triggers a visual LED warning, sounds an audible buzzer alert, and displays real-time status updates on a 16x2 I2C LCD screen.
problemStatement: Gas leaks in kitchens, laboratories, and industrial environments pose severe health hazards and fire risks. Early detection of toxic or flammable gases is critical to prevent accidents.
solutionApproach: An automated Arduino-based Gas Detection System that continuously reads analog values from an MQ-135 gas sensor, displays live concentration readings on an LCD screen, and immediately triggers visual and audible alarms if gas levels cross safe thresholds.
circuitDiagramDescription: The MQ-135 sensor's analog pin A0 connects to Arduino A0. The I2C LCD module connects to 5V, GND, SDA (A4), and SCL (A5). The Buzzer connects to Digital Pin D8 and GND, while the LED connects to Digital Pin D9.

working.action: The Arduino initializes the I2C 16x2 LCD and warms up the MQ-135 gas sensor for 3 seconds.
The MQ-135 sensor measures ambient air quality and sends an analog gas concentration reading to pin A0.
Arduino displays the real-time gas value on Row 1 of the LCD display.
If the gas value exceeds the threshold (150), Arduino turns ON the Buzzer (Pin 8) and Red LED (Pin 9), displaying '!ALERT!' on the screen.
If gas concentration is normal, the Buzzer and LED remain OFF, displaying 'SAFE' status.

title: LiFi Secure Terminal
subtitle: Visible Light Optical Communication PWA & Arduino Receiver for EMI-Sensitive Environments
author: Tinkering Lab
desc: High-security visible light optical transmitter PWA using smartphone screen flash or flashlight torch paired with an Arduino Uno mid-bit sampling receiver.
fullDesc: The LiFi Secure Terminal is a complete Visible Light Communication (VLC) system designed for environments where Radio Frequency (RF) emissions are strictly prohibited or compromised (such as Intensive Care Units, defense command centers, aircraft cabins, and underground bunkers). The system features a mobile-first Progressive Web Application (PWA) with a camera-free optical screen flash pad and optional camera torch controller to transmit binary optical data using 10 Hz pulse duration framing (Start bit 1, 8 Data bits MSB-first, Stop bit 0). Includes doctor/ICU presets and quick chat message chips ('hello', 'how are you', 'what you see', 'STAT: ICU BED 4'). On the receiving end, an Arduino Uno with an LDR Digital Module captures light pulses using a 1.5x bit period (150 ms) mid-bit sampling technique to eliminate edge jitter and decodes real-time ASCII messages onto a 16x2 I2C LCD screen.
problemStatement: Radio frequency communications (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Cellular) generate Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) that disrupts medical equipment in ICUs and presents severe RF signal interception risks in secure defense installations.
solutionApproach: An optical LiFi transceiver system using light waves. The transmitter encodes custom text or medical presets into 8-bit ASCII binary frames with framing bits (Start=1, Stop=0) and modulates light pulses via smartphone screen flash or torch. The Arduino receiver detects incoming optical pulses, synchronizes on the rising edge of the Start bit, delays 150 ms to align dead-center inside the first payload bit, and samples subsequent bits every 100 ms to reconstruct ASCII characters for real-time LCD rendering.

hardwareSpecs.sensorModule: LDR Light Dependent Resistor Sensor Module with LM393 Comparator
hardwareSpecs.display: 16x2 Character LCD with PCF8574 I2C Backpack (Address 0x27)
hardwareSpecs.transmitter: Mobile Device Screen Flash / Rear Camera Flashlight

components: LDR Sensor Module with Digital Output (D0)
circuitDiagramDescription: The LDR Sensor Module's digital output D0 connects to Arduino Digital Pin 8. The 16x2 I2C LCD display connects to 5V, GND, SDA (Analog Pin A4), and SCL (Analog Pin A5). Sensitivity threshold is tuned via the LM393 potentiometer on the LDR board.

working.action: The user selects a medical/doctor preset ('STAT: ICU BED 4', 'BP NORMAL 120/80'), chat preset ('hello', 'how are you', 'what you see'), or types a custom message.
The mobile PWA converts text payload into 8-bit ASCII binary bytes with 10-bit framing (Start Bit 1, 8 Data Bits MSB-first, Stop Bit 0).
The optical screen flash pad (or optional torch) pulses light at 100 ms per bit directly onto the LDR sensor lens.
The Arduino receiver monitors Pin 8 for the rising edge of the optical Start Bit (LIGHT_ON).
Upon detecting the Start Bit, the Arduino waits 150 ms (1.5x bit period) to position the sensor reading dead-center in the middle of Data Bit 7 (MSB).
The receiver samples Data Bit 7, then loops 7 times at exact 100 ms intervals to sample Data Bits 6 through 0, assembling the byte.
Valid ASCII characters (range 32 to 126) are dynamically displayed on Line 2 of the 16x2 LCD screen.
If no light signal is received for 4000 ms, the system automatically resets the screen buffer back to 'Listening...'.

benefits: Zero RF emissions - safe for ICUs and explosive zones
Camera-free screen optical flash pulser - zero browser permission popups required
Includes medical/ICU doctor presets and quick chat message chips
Mid-bit sampling eliminates timing jitter and signal edge distortion
Configurable sensor logic (supports both Active-HIGH and Active-LOW LDR modules)
Real-time 16x2 LCD receiver simulator on the webpage
futureScope: Implement Manchester Encoding to eliminate DC bias and enable clock recovery.
Add Error Detection & Correction (Reed-Solomon or CRC-8 checksums).
Upgrade to array photodiode receiver for multi-color RGB wavelength division multiplexing (WDM).

vivaQuestions.q: Why is 1.5x bit period delay (150 ms) used after detecting the Start Bit?
vivaQuestions.a: The 1.5x bit period delay aligns the sampling instant directly at the center of the first payload bit (100 ms start bit + 50 ms to center of first bit), preventing errors caused by edge rise-time jitter.

vivaQuestions.q: What is the role of the LM393 comparator on the LDR sensor module?
vivaQuestions.a: The LM393 compares the analog voltage from the LDR against a potentiometer threshold to produce a clean binary digital square wave (D0 pin).

vivaQuestions.q: How does the code handle inverted (active-LOW) light sensors?
vivaQuestions.a: The code uses macro normalization: `#define LIGHT_ON LOW`. Changing line 8 to `#define LIGHT_ON LOW` flips all internal detection logic effortlessly.

vivaQuestions.q: What framing format is used for transmitting each ASCII character?
vivaQuestions.a: 1 Start Bit (HIGH) + 8 Data Bits (MSB-first) + 1 Stop Bit (LOW), resulting in 10 bits total per character.

fullDesc: This project demonstrates the interfacing of a Single Common Cathode 7-Segment Display with an Arduino Uno using the Wokwi Simulator. It helps students understand digital outputs, circuit connections, Arduino programming, and display interfacing by displaying numbers from 0 to 9 sequentially. The project is designed for beginners and provides practical exposure to embedded systems and digital electronics without requiring physical hardware.
author: Sujal Prasad

team.name: Anushka Varma
team.role: Project Lead & Embedded Systems Developer (Class IX)

innovation: This project simplifies the understanding of digital display interfacing by using the Wokwi Simulator, allowing students to learn Arduino programming, circuit connections, and embedded systems concepts without requiring physical hardware.
problemStatement: Students often find it difficult to understand how a 7-Segment Display communicates with a microcontroller. Learning digital electronics, Arduino programming, and circuit connections becomes challenging without practical demonstrations.
solutionApproach: The project interfaces a Single Common Cathode 7-Segment Display with an Arduino Uno. Using Arduino digital output pins, individual display segments are controlled to sequentially display digits from 0 to 9. The Wokwi Simulator provides a safe and interactive environment for learning and experimentation.
guide: Connect the 7-Segment Display to the Arduino Uno according to the circuit diagram.
Connect the Common Cathode (COM) pin to GND.
Upload the Arduino program in the Wokwi Simulator.
Run the simulation.
Observe the display counting from 0 to 9.
Verify that the Decimal Point (DP) remains ON throughout the sequence.

title: Smart Bridge for Flood Safety
subtitle: Automatic Bridge Lift System Using Water Level Detection

problem.title: Increasing River Water Level During Heavy Rainfall
problem.description: During heavy rainfall, the river water level rises rapidly and floods low-level bridges. Students, office workers, emergency services, and vehicles are unable to cross the bridge safely. Many people remain stranded for hours or even days, causing delays, accidents, and disruption of essential services.

solution.title: Smart Automatic Bridge
solution.description: A smart bridge continuously monitors the river water level using a water level sensor. When the water reaches a dangerous level, the bridge automatically lifts upward, preventing vehicles and people from entering the flooded area. At the same time, a buzzer sounds and an LED glows to warn everyone nearby. Once the water level becomes safe, the bridge returns to its normal position.

working.action: Water level sensor continuously measures the river water level.
If the water level exceeds the safe limit, the controller activates the system.
A servo motor lifts the bridge automatically.
The buzzer starts beeping and the LED glows to alert people.
When the water level drops below the danger level, the bridge lowers automatically and traffic resumes safely.

benefits: Prevents accidents during floods.
Provides early warning to people.
Protects students, vehicles, and pedestrians.
Supports emergency services with timely information.
Reduces traffic disruption caused by flooded bridges.
Improves public safety in flood-prone areas.
futureScope: Send SMS alerts to nearby residents.
Display water level information on an LED display board.
Connect with a mobile application for live monitoring.
Integrate with weather forecasting systems.
Upload real-time bridge status to the cloud using IoT.
Install CCTV cameras for remote monitoring.

impact.community: Improves public safety and reduces the risk of flood-related accidents.
impact.environment: Encourages safe disaster management without harming the environment.
impact.social: Helps people travel safely and reduces panic during floods.

title: Home Automation using Arduino IR Remote Control Sensor | Smart Home
subtitle: Control Home Appliances with an IR Remote and Arduino UNO
desc: Build a smart home automation system using an Arduino UNO, IR Remote, and Relay Module to control electrical appliances wirelessly.
fullDesc: This project demonstrates a simple and affordable home automation system using an Arduino UNO and an IR Remote Control. The Arduino receives commands from the IR receiver sensor and controls electrical appliances through a relay module. It introduces students to wireless communication, embedded systems, and smart home technology.
author: Dipavalee Sudrik
innovation: A low-cost smart home automation solution that enables wireless appliance control using an IR remote and Arduino, making home automation affordable for students and beginners.
problemStatement: Traditional electrical switches require manual operation and are not convenient for elderly people, people with disabilities, or users seeking smart home functionality.
solutionApproach: An Arduino UNO receives signals from an IR receiver sensor connected to an IR remote. Based on the received command, the Arduino switches the relay ON or OFF, allowing household electrical appliances such as lamps or bulbs to be controlled wirelessly.
guide: Connect the IR Receiver VCC to Arduino 5V.
Connect the IR Receiver GND to Arduino GND.
Connect the IR Receiver OUT pin to Arduino Digital Pin 2.
Connect the Relay Module IN pin to Arduino Digital Pin 13.
Connect Relay VCC to Arduino 5V and GND to Arduino GND.
Connect the Lamp Holder through the Relay Module following proper electrical safety guidelines.
Connect the Arduino UNO to the computer using a USB cable.
Open Arduino IDE and paste the provided Arduino code.
Upload the program to the Arduino UNO.
Point the IR Remote toward the IR Receiver and press Button 1 to turn the lamp ON or OFF.

title: Smart Parking System

desc: Detect car presence with IR sensors — control entry with a servo!
fullDesc: Build a smart parking system that uses 6 IR sensors to detect occupied and free slots, controls entry/exit with a servo motor barrier, and displays real-time slot availability on a display.

innovation: Low-cost parking management prototype using IR-based slot detection and automated barrier control, suitable for school labs and demo environments.
problemStatement: Manual parking management is inefficient and prone to errors. There is no easy way to know slot availability without physically checking each space.
solutionApproach: Used 6 IR sensors to detect car presence in each slot, a servo motor as an entry/exit barrier, and a display to show live slot availability — all controlled by an Arduino UNO.

hardwareSpecs.communicationProtocol: Digital I/O (IR sensors), PWM (Servo), I2C or 4-bit parallel (Display)

guide: Connect each IR sensor OUT pin to Arduino digital pins D2–D7; VCC to 5V, GND to GND
Connect servo signal wire to Arduino D9 (PWM pin); VCC to 5V, GND to GND
Wire LCD in 4-bit mode: RS→D10, EN→D11, D4-D7→D12-D13 (adjust as needed)
Connect potentiometer wiper to LCD V0 pin for contrast control
Install the Servo library (built-in) and LiquidCrystal library via Arduino IDE Library Manager
Upload the starter sketch and open Serial Monitor at 9600 baud
Place 3D printed cars in front of IR sensors to simulate parked vehicles
Verify slot detection in Serial Monitor; observe servo opening/closing on entry trigger
Confirm display shows correct free/occupied slot count
prerequisites: Understanding of digital I/O and PWM

title: Smart Vacuum Cleaner

problemStatement: Manual floor cleaning is time-consuming and requires continuous human effort. An affordable automated cleaning solution can improve efficiency while helping students learn robotics and automation.
solutionApproach: The robot uses an ultrasonic sensor to detect obstacles and an Arduino UNO to control movement through an L293D motor driver. A high-speed fan creates suction to collect dust while the robot automatically navigates the floor.

Step 4: Install the vacuum fan and dust collection chamber.

title: VASC Age
subtitle: Pulse-based vascular age estimation using MAX30102
desc: Measure your pulse â€” estimate your vascular age over WiFi!
fullDesc: Build a smart health-monitoring device that reads pulse and blood-oxygen data from a MAX30102 sensor via an ESP8266, then serves live readings and an estimated vascular age to a web dashboard over WiFi â€” no app installation required.
author: Shruti Mestry
innovation: A low-cost, WiFi-connected vascular age estimator that turns raw pulse-oximetry data into an accessible health metric, viewable from any browser on the local network.
problemStatement: Vascular age and pulse health monitoring devices are often expensive or require dedicated apps, making them inaccessible for students and hobbyists wanting to learn practical health-tech.
solutionApproach: Used a MAX30102 pulse-oximetry sensor connected to an ESP8266 over I2C. The ESP8266 connects to WiFi, continuously reads sensor data via a SensorManager module, and serves live readings through a lightweight built-in web server (WebManager), removing the need for a companion app.

title: Smart Vertical Axis Wind Turbine
subtitle: Kinetic harvesting with automatic dark-activated indicator
desc: Build an omnidirectional wind turbine that generates power and senses ambient light!
fullDesc: Build a functional Vertical Axis Wind Turbine (VAWT) using a Savonius rotor to drive a DC dynamo motor generator, paired with a BC547 transistor circuit that automatically triggers an indicator when night falls...
author: Siddharth
innovation: An omnidirectional wind harvester integrated with an automatic light-sensing emergency load circuit for school yard applications.
problemStatement: Standard clean energy setups require manual switching or expensive digital controllers to manage stored energy or trigger night indicators.
solutionApproach: Utilized a high-efficiency vertical drag rotor coupled with a DC dynamo motor to harvest wind energy into a DC battery bank. Integrated an analog BC547 NPN transistor switching circuit with an LDR to automatically engage low-power indicators based on ambient light conditions.

hardwareSpecs.powerConsumption: Idle: ~0.5mA, Active Generation: Variable based on wind speed

guide: Assemble the vertical rotor blades onto the central shaft and couple it directly to the axle of the DC dynamo motor.
Connect the positive output of the dynamo motor through a protection diode to the positive terminal of the DC Battery to store generated power safely.
Place the BC547 NPN transistor on the breadboard (Pins: Emitter, Base, Collector).
Connect the 100kΩ resistor from the positive battery rail to the Base pin of the BC547 transistor.
Connect the LDR sensor between the Base pin of the BC547 transistor and the Ground/Negative battery rail to form a voltage divider.
Connect an indicator LED (with appropriate current resistor) or secondary load from the Positive rail to the Collector pin of the transistor.
Connect the Emitter pin of the BC547 directly to the Ground/Negative rail.
Spin the wind turbine to confirm battery charging, and cover the LDR sensor to test the automatic dark-activated switching mechanism.
